claims.summary: Finite configuration, Fejer kernel K_L, off-line pairs gamma_j +- i delta_j of multiplicity m_j: (a) D_off(tau) >= - sum m_j e^{delta_j L} min(2L, 8/(L((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta_j^2))), so if all delta_j <= theta and theta L >= 2 the density is at least -8 M e^{theta L}/(L theta^2); (b) with delta* the largest distance and tau off the heights and midpoints of the pairs at delta*, for every L_1 some L > L_1 has D_L(tau) <= -q' e^{delta* L}/L, q' < q = sum |c_j|^2/(2 sum |c_j|), c_j = m_j/(tau - gamma_j - i delta*)^2; hence D_L(tau) >= -C e^{theta L} for all large L forces delta* <= theta.

claims.rationale: Shows that the one-sided premise for all lengths is, in the model, the statement that no pair is farther than theta from the line.

claims.summary: I(a) = (1/a) int_a^{2a} log|2 cos u| du >= -2 for every a > 0; hence for P(y) = prod_{i<=n} (1 + e^{-i y eta_i}), eta_i > 0 (nonnegative integer coefficients, sum M = 2^n) and every L_0 > 0, the mean of log|P| over [L_0, 2 L_0] is at least -2n and sup over that interval of |P|/M is at least M^{-1 - 2/log 2}.

claims.rationale: Bounds how deeply a product family, the known way of hiding a cluster on a range of lengths, can hide: by a fixed power of its total multiplicity.
